I downloaded Wild Animal Racing as a joke. That was the last joke I ever told. The moment I launched the game, I was greeted by what can only be described as a cursed hallucination of a giraffe with dead eyes and a hunger for victory. I picked the elephant because he looked like he knew pain, and I needed a guide. The race began and suddenly I was in Egypt, then Paris, then the Arctic—was I traveling through time? Was the rhino behind me or was he inside me spiritually? The controls are like driving a shopping cart down a mountain during an earthquake but somehow that only adds to the transcendence. The music is what I imagine plays in the waiting room of a dentist in purgatory. I threw a rocket at a lion and he spun so fast the laws of physics asked for a break. The giraffe overtook me at the last second and I swear he whispered “your soul is mine” before crossing the finish line. I cried. I laughed. I became something more than human. At one point my computer crashed and rebooted to find Wild Animal Racing still running, uninvited, in the background, like it wanted me to keep playing. My dog no longer trusts me. My spouse left a note that simply said “you’ve changed.” I have. I have seen the polygonal gates of madness and driven a hippo through them at 40km/h. This isn’t a game. This is a rite of passage. Buy it. Gift it. Let it consume you like it consumed me.

Before playing Wild Animal Racing by Paul Bird, I wandered through life aimlessly, unsure of my purpose or direction. But the moment I fired up this game, everything changed.

Guiding a giraffe through treacherous tracks while dodging bizarre obstacles may sound like simple fun, but it’s so much more. The game’s quirky charm, vibrant visuals, and unapologetically wacky mechanics awakened something profound within me. Each race felt like a metaphor for life—teaching me to persevere through chaos, adapt to unexpected twists, and celebrate the small victories.

The multiplayer feature brought me closer to friends and strangers alike, fostering bonds I didn’t know I needed. The whimsical soundtrack? Pure therapy for the soul. The sound design? Pleasure for the ears.

Then there are the movies—a delightful surprise that showcases the technology behind the game. It’s a glimpse into its innovative spirit, clearly ahead of its time and brimming with unrestrained creativity.

Wild Animal Racing isn’t just a game; it’s an experience, a guide, and a reason to keep racing forward in life. Paul Bird, you’ve created a masterpiece. Thank you for changing my life.
